correctness.rationale: For n≥2 the uniform rooted ordered full binary tree root split has P(K=i)=C_i C_(n−1−i)/C_n. Cherry enumerator A(z)=z/sqrt(1−4z), Catalan F=1+zF². Extracting coefficients of (zF′)² and 2(zA′)(zF′), including n=2, yields Cov(X,B)=(n−2)4^(n−1)/[4(2n−1)C_n]; Q=(n−1)²−4B gives Cov(X,Q)=−(n−2)4^(n−1)/[(2n−1)C_n]. Bivariate cherry GF G=1+z(G²−1+u) gives Var(X)=n(n−2)(n−1)(n+1)/[2(2n−3)(2n−1)²] and Catalan split bulk asymptotics with endpoint truncation give Var(B)~sqrt(pi)n^(7/2)/32; combining gives Corr(X,Q)~−pi^(1/4)/sqrt(2)n^(−3/4) only for n≥3. Independently exhaustively enumerated plane full binary trees n=2..9, checking X,B,Q moments with exact rational arithmetic; no claim enumeration proves the all-n theorem.
residual_risks: n=2 has deterministic X, so the claimed correlation is undefined there; theorem correctly excludes it.
Bulk split asymptotic needs endpoint control; accepted using uniform C_j=O(4^j/(j+1)^(3/2)) and tail truncation, not finite fitting.

value.rationale: Cherries measure local branching, whereas squared root imbalance measures global top split. An exact sign for all n≥3 together with a decaying normalized correlation quantifies dependence of two standard tree-shape observables and gives the full conditional split regression; this is more than a textbook marginal count or arbitrary tiny case.
